transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-12-03 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Alex Choi (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Aurelia Head of Search), Maya Singh (Aurelia ML Eng), Carlos Ruiz (Aurelia Infra)

[00:00] Alex Choi: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm alex from redwood, with priya on the call to dig into architecture and perf.
[00:18] Jordan Kim: thanks alex, um yeah we wanted to focus on embeddings and rerank. the context: we run a customer support search across europe and na, about 18M docs, avg doc length 1-2 paragraphs, peak queries about 800 qps but with strong spikes to 2k for specific campaigns.
[00:38] Priya Patel: ok got it. is this currently using an external vector DB or in-house solution?
[00:45] Maya Singh: we have a homegrown FAISS cluster, sharded by customer id, but it's gotten brittle — especially around rebalancing and node failures. also, latency is spiky; p95 220ms for nearest neighbors plus the reranker.
[01:05] Carlos Ruiz: infra-wise we're on managed k8s with EBS-backed instances, limited GPU budget; exploring both hosted and dedicated solutions. security: SOC2 in place, we need SSO, KMS, and VPC peering for private deployments.
[01:30] Alex Choi: that's the typical trade. for clarity: are you considering Redwood Hosted first for PoC and then Dedicated/Private for production?
[01:40] Jordan Kim: yeah hosted for a quick PoC, but for sustained traffic we lean toward Dedicated or Private because of cost predictability and data residency.
[01:52] Priya Patel: on embeddings, what's your current dimensionality and indexing config?
[01:57] Maya Singh: we're running 768-d vectors, HNSW index in FAISS with efSearch=128, M=32. we see recall@10 around 0.82 on our dev set but reranker (a 3B model) adds ~80ms.
[02:18] Priya Patel: good baseline. two levers we often discuss: increase vector dim to 1536 for better semantic fidelity but more throughput cost; or keep 768 and tune ANN params + use lexical hybrid signals.
[02:36] Jordan Kim: curious if you recommend hybrid search — we have strong keyword signals in titles and metadata.
[02:42] Alex Choi: yes, hybrid is common — candidate retrieval via ANN and a lightweight BM25 or metadata filter before rerank. Redwood supports rerank pipelines where the candidate set size is configurable; typical candidate size is 50-200.
[03:00] [03:00] Speaker 1: uh-huh, got it.
[03:10] Maya Singh: one concern — our index is 18M vectors; storage and network egress matter. any guidance on vector compression or quantization?
[03:20] Priya Patel: we support recommending quantization profiles; for example 8-bit PQ or OPQ to shrink size ~4x for 1536->effective footprint. that interacts with recall; we usually run a quant-aware eval.
[03:36] Alex Choi: also K/V cache and prefix caching can cut repeated reranker calls for similar queries; that helps cost and latency for hot queries.
[03:50] Jordan Kim: when you say "we recommend" — is that in the Optimize product or part of Professional Services?
[03:58] Priya Patel: both. Optimize gives automated suggestions and simulated tradeoffs; for a production rollout we can do a hands-on tuning with our SEs.
[04:08] Carlos Ruiz: from infra perspective: if we go Dedicated, how does sharding and replication work across AZs? we need cross-region read replicas for eu and na.
[04:18] Priya Patel: Dedicated lets you configure GPU pools per region; the control plane can route requests by policy. For vector stores we recommend either logical sharding by namespace with replication, or a global index with region-local replicas — both patterns are supported but tradeoffs differ: global index simplifies freshness, local replicas cut latency and egress.
[04:40] Jordan Kim: can you run the numbers for cost and latency for 768 vs 1536 dims given 800 qps baseline and spike to 2k?
[04:48] Alex Choi: yes — action item. we'll run sims. Priya, we'll need batch size assumptions and reranker per-call cost.
[04:56] Priya Patel: for embeddings-only stage: with 768 dims, CPU+ANN can handle >5k qps with adequate sharding. Reranker at 3B model on GPU is the blocker — we typically convert into an async rerank or a two-stage lighter-weight reranker for latency-sensitive flows.
[05:18] Maya Singh: our current reranker is fairly heavy; we could try a distilled 1.3B or run rerank as background scoring for non-real-time channels.
[05:26] [05:26] Jordan Kim: question on metrics — we measure MRR and recall@10; what thresholds should we set to consider migrating to Dedicated?
[05:34] Priya Patel: generally customers migrate when p95 latency on user-visible flows is >200ms or cost per query on hosted grows beyond thresholds. Also SLA needs and compliance (VPC/KMS) push for Dedicated/Private.
[05:48] Alex Choi: quick note on fallback: Redwood can route to smaller models or cached responses when capacity hits limits; graceful degradation is built-in.
[05:58] Carlos Ruiz: ok, security — what are the integration points for KMS and audit logs?
[06:04] Alex Choi: we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/HSM) for Private; audit logs include per-request metadata, and console exposes token-level billing. we'll share SOC2 and network diagrams.
[06:18] Maya Singh: awesome. also, what's the expected indexing pipeline? we ingest nightly deltas of ~300k docs; real-time updates are rare but critical for some keys.
[06:30] Priya Patel: that's common — we recommend a hybrid approach: batch rebuilds nightly and streaming upserts for hot records. It affects shard design and memory footprint.
[06:42] Jordan Kim: can Redwood run an eval on our 1k query sample to show recall + rerank lift?
[06:48] Alex Choi: yes we'll run an end-to-end eval using your sample queries; need your labels and acceptance criteria.
[06:56] [06:56] Speaker 2: mm-hmm.
[07:06] Maya Singh: what about vector DB options — is Redwood tied to one or can you integrate with our FAISS/milvus/pinecone?
[07:14] Priya Patel: we integrate with multiple backends. Hosted uses our managed ANN layer; for Dedicated/Private, you can bring your own vector store — we support connectors for FAISS, Milvus, Andromeda-compatible APIs, and can proxy to remote Faiss clusters.
[07:32] Carlos Ruiz: network egress costs are a worry. if vectors live in our VPC and Redwood in-hosted, how does that flow?
[07:40] Alex Choi: for Hosted, typical pattern is customers upload embeddings to Redwood-managed stores (ingest over TLS). For Private you bring your data in your VPC. For Dedicated we offer options: isolated storage in customer's VPC peered with Redwood control plane, or managed storage with encryption and restricted subnets. We'll detail cost models.
[08:02] Jordan Kim: let's talk SLOs — what latency can we expect for 50-candidate rerank with 3B model on Dedicated GPUs?
[08:10] Priya Patel: ballpark: 50 candidates reranked with a 3B model ~80-140ms on a modern A10/A100 equivalent depending on batch (we often batch rerank calls to amortize model load). If you need sub-100ms consistently, consider a distilled reranker at 1.3B or fewer candidates.
[08:32] Maya Singh: and throughput — gpu limits aside, how many reranks/sec can we get per GPU?
[08:36] Priya Patel: rough numbers: 3B model ~150-300 reranks/s per GPU with small batch optimization; 1.3B ~400-1200 reranks/s. we'll simulate with your candidate sizes.
[08:52] Alex Choi: note that batching helps, but it increases tail latency for single requests. it's a tradeoff.
[08:59] Jordan Kim: on eval metrics, we want to see recall lift of at least +0.05 and MRR improvement for the reranker to be considered.
[09:06] [09:06] Speaker 1: okay
[09:16] Maya Singh: one more infra question: how do upgrades/rollouts work for Private deployments? we need canary and rollback for model and infra changes.
[09:26] Priya Patel: Private includes our control plane for orchestration; you can pin model versions, do canary rollouts and automated rollback on error budgets. We log per-request traces to help debugging.
[09:38] Carlos Ruiz: for our FAISS migration, what's the recommended shard size? we currently have 18M vectors; should we do 1M per shard or larger?
[09:48] Priya Patel: shard size depends on query distribution and memory. For HNSW, keeping shards ~1-4M is common to keep graph memory reasonable; if you need dense recall, smaller shards with aggregation across replicas works better. We'll look at your QPS distribution.
[10:06] Alex Choi: also consider namespace-level TTL for ephemeral documents to avoid large rebuilds.
[10:12] Jordan Kim: costs — can you give a rough hosted pricing estimate for 800 qps baseline with rerank on 1.3B model?
[10:22] Alex Choi: we'll provide a modeled spreadsheet (actionable). high level: tokens for rerank + vector ops; but we prefer to give a tailored estimate after we run throughput sims.
[10:34] [10:34] Speaker 2: okay thanks
[10:44] Maya Singh: we have a few constraints: max per-request latency target 150ms p95 for web UI; offline channels can be relaxed. Also must keep PII encrypted and not log user text in clear.
[10:58] Alex Choi: we can redact PII at ingest or use edge transformations; compliance-wise, Private gives strongest guarantees.
[11:08] Jordan Kim: curious about cold-start and index rebuild times — for a full rebuild of 18M vectors, what are we looking at?
[11:16] Priya Patel: depends on hardware; with a dedicated GPU indexing pipeline and parallel workers, roughly hours (2-6h) for full rebuilds; with incremental updates nightly it's sped up. We'll include best practices doc.
[11:30] Carlos Ruiz: network and storage: we need estimates of storage footprint for 768 vs 1536 dims with quantization options.
[11:38] Alex Choi: action: we'll include a small table in the spreadsheet: raw size, PQ-compressed size, expected RAM for HNSW, and disk for backups.
[11:50] Maya Singh: ok good. about proving quality: can Redwood run an A/B where we keep current FAISS plus Redwood rerank to compare metrics?
[11:58] Priya Patel: yes, we can run shadow traffic or side-by-side rerank experiments. We'll propose a PoC that does candidate retrieval via your FAISS and rerank via Redwood Hosted first.
[12:10] Jordan Kim: timeline — we want to ship a PoC within 3 weeks. feasible?
[12:16] Alex Choi: yes if we get samples and the test harness ASAP. propose a 3-week plan: week 1 integrate embeddings/keys, week 2 run eval and tune ANN params, week 3 run live traffic and measure.
[12:30] Maya Singh: sounds tight but doable.
[12:36] Carlos Ruiz: any blockers on our side? network peering for Dedicated might take time — 2-3 weeks for infra approvals.
[12:44] Alex Choi: we'll start with Hosted PoC to parallelize approvals.
[12:50] [12:50] Speaker 3: thanks
[13:02] Priya Patel: recap of technical asks: we need sample queries + labels, QPS heatmap, confirmation of whether you'll try 768->1536, and infra constraints. We'll run sims for reranker throughput and candidate sizes.
[13:18] Jordan Kim: i'll send sample queries (Maya will extract) and causal acceptance criteria.
[13:26] Alex Choi: next steps recap: spreadsheet + docs from us, scheduled pricing follow-up, and a kickoff once the PoC contract is signed.
[13:40] Maya Singh: any immediate concerns with bringing our FAISS into Redwood?
[13:46] Priya Patel: no blockers; we may recommend migrating to managed ANN for easier autoscaling but can connect to FAISS for PoC.
[13:56] Jordan Kim: great. thanks everyone.
[14:00] Alex Choi: thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials by end of week.

Shared links referenced: 1) Benchmark spreadsheet (link sent after call) 2) SOC2 + Private deployment checklist (link) 3) PoC contract template (link)

End of transcript.
